mechanism_narrative: Accelerating GDP growth, as measured by the year-over-year change in real GDP, signals a strengthening economy that will boost corporate earnings and drive positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Yield curve inverts (10y-2y < 0) during the signal period, indicating a looming recession that will negate the positive earnings impulse.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in industrial production, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in unemployment, signals a positive supply shock that will boost productivity and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO declines > 0.5% m/m and UNRATE does not rise
failure_condition: SPX realizes negative 20-day returns in > 60% of instances where the positive supply shock signal is triggered.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate, if accompanied by stable or falling consumer prices, signals a disinflationary labor market shock that will allow the Fed to ease policy and boost S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months and CPIAUCSL does not rise
failure_condition: Fed funds rate rises > 25bp in the month following the signal trigger, indicating that the disinflationary shock was not sufficient to shift policy.

mechanism_narrative: A surge in housing starts, if accompanied by a rise in consumer confidence, signals a positive demand shock that will boost economic growth and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST rises > 5% y/y and RSAFS rises > 10% y/y
failure_condition: Leading economic indicators (e.g., yield curve slope, manufacturing PMI) turn negative during the signal period, indicating an impending growth slowdown.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in the federal funds rate, if not accompanied by a contemporaneous rise in consumer prices, signals a positive real rates shock that will boost the value of the dollar and depress S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises > 50bp in 3 months and CPIAUCSL does not rise
failure_condition: DXY (US dollar index) falls > 2% in the month following the signal trigger, indicating that the real rates shock was not sufficient to boost the dollar.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in payroll employment, if accompanied by a rise in the unemployment rate, signals a negative labor market shock that will depress consumer spending and S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS declines > 100k m/m and UNRATE rises > 0.2pp
failure_condition: Consumer confidence (e.g., Michigan survey) rises > 2pts in the month following the signal trigger, indicating that the labor market shock was not sufficiently severe to depress spending.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in industrial production, if accompanied by stable or falling unemployment, signals a positive supply-side shock that will boost productivity and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: Core PPI (producer price index) rises > 3% y/y during the signal period, indicating that the supply-side shock is actually inflationary.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in real GDP, if accompanied by a rise in the unemployment rate, signals a negative demand shock that will depress corporate earnings and S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 declines > 1% q/q and UNRATE rises > 0.3pp
failure_condition: Equity fund flows turn sharply positive (> $10bn inflows) in the month following the signal trigger, indicating that investors are dismissing the demand shock as transitory.
